title: Muscle
description: A named muscle, decomposed into one or more functional compartments (neuromuscular partitions). Each compartment carries a parametric fiber-architecture description consumed by engine/fiber_field.py to procedurally generate a 1mm-resolution vector field of individual fascicle centerlines between origin and insertion surfaces — this is how per-fiber-bundle direction and per-compartment grouping is produced without hand-authoring millions of fiber curves.

via_points.description: Wrapping/via points (retinacula, bony pulleys, sesamoids) the muscle-tendon path is constrained through, so its path deforms plausibly rather than penetrating bone during joint rotation.

bone_frame.description: id of the bone whose local frame this via-point is rigidly attached to

functional_compartments.description: Independently-innervated or mechanically-separable fiber bundle groups within this single named muscle (e.g. deltoid's ~7 segments, biceps femoris' two heads). A muscle with a single homogeneous fiber population still gets exactly one compartment entry.

innervation_branch.description: specific nerve branch/twig serving only this compartment, when documented

aponeurosis_definition.description: how the internal aponeurosis surface(s) that fibers attach to are defined, for pennate muscles

fiber_field_seed_region_local_mm.description: Polygon (list of vec3_mm, in origin_bone's local frame) bounding the origin footprint of this compartment's fibers on the origin surface — the seed curve fiber_field.py sows fascicle start points along.

neuromuscular_junction_zone.description: The NMJ/motor endplate band is a localized transverse zone (not point-uniform) documented for most human muscles, typically near the fascicle midpoint / muscle belly center.

position_fraction_along_fascicle.description: 0=origin end, 1=insertion end; ~0.5 for most parallel/fusiform muscles per endplate-banding studies

band_width_fraction.description: width of the endplate zone as a fraction of total fascicle length
